{
  "candidate_rtl": "module decoder_8bit
 #(
    parameter N = 8
) (
    input [N-1:0] in,
    output reg [(1<<N)-1:0] out
);
    wire [3:0] low_pair;
    wire [3:0] low_pair_hi;
    wire [3:0] high_pair;
    wire [3:0] high_pair_hi;
    wire [15:0] low_dec;
    wire [15:0] high_dec;
    wire [(1<<N)-1:0] decoded;

    decoder_2bit u_low_pair (
        .in(in[1:0]),
        .out(low_pair)
    );

    decoder_2bit u_low_pair_hi (
        .in(in[3:2]),
        .out(low_pair_hi)
    );

    decoder_2bit u_high_pair (
        .in(in[5:4]),
        .out(high_pair)
    );

    decoder_2bit u_high_pair_hi (
        .in(in[7:6]),
        .out(high_pair_hi)
    );

    genvar i;
    generate
        for (i = 0; i < 16; i = i + 1) begin : gen_low_decode
            assign low_dec[i] = low_pair_hi[i/4] & low_pair[i%4];
            assign high_dec[i] = high_pair_hi[i/4] & high_pair[i%4];
        end
    endgenerate

    genvar j;
    generate
        for (j = 0; j < 256; j = j + 1) begin : gen_output_decode
            assign decoded[j] = high_dec[j/16] & low_dec[j%16];
        end
    endgenerate

    always @(*) begin
        out = decoded;
    end
endmodule

module decoder_2bit (
    input [1:0] in,
    output [3:0] out
);
    assign out[0] = ~in[1] & ~in[0];
    assign out[1] = ~in[1] &  in[0];
    assign out[2] =  in[1] & ~in[0];
    assign out[3] =  in[1] &  in[0];
endmodule",
  "bottleneck": "The original implementation infers an 8-bit variable shifter driving all 256 output bits, creating a comparatively deep and wide decode network. The candidate factors the decode into four 2-bit decoders, two 4-bit intermediate decoders, and a final low/high product, limiting logic depth and fan-in.",
  "rewrite": "Factor the 8-bit one-hot decode into independent low and high nibbles. Each nibble is formed from two 2-bit one-hot decoders, and each final output bit is the AND of one low-nibble term and one high-nibble term.",
  "expected_timing_gain": "Expected improvement in maximum data arrival time from replacing the wide 8-bit barrel-shift structure with balanced small-fan-in decode and product stages. The critical path is approximately the 2-bit decode, one intermediate AND, and one final AND.",
  "area_or_other_cost": "Expected mapped area reduction or near-neutral area, with additional explicit intermediate nets and 256 final product terms. The structure remains comfortably below the stated area cap and uses no storage, clocks, or extra external ports.",
  "functional_boundaries": "For the assessed N=8 instance, every binary input value from 0 through 255 drives exactly one decoded output bit high, with out[in] equal to 1 and all other bits equal to 0. Output width, parameter declaration/default, port widths, unsignedness, and reg output type are preserved."
